correctness.rationale: For p,q>=3 and c>=0, orthogonal decomposition yields A-prime/B-prime zero-sum eigenspaces of dimensions p-2 and q-2 plus a four-orbit quotient. Exact determinant evaluations show residual quotient eigenvalues are disjoint from p and q when p!=q and c!=1. For p=q and c!=1 the combined eigenvalue-n space has the three stated linear constraints and dimension 2n-3; the omitted-coordinate count establishes necessary and sufficient observation. At c=1, complete-bipartite zero-sum eigenspaces require all but one leader per full part. PBH yields all three criteria, and direct weighted subset enumeration yields the generating polynomials. Actual standalone Python check completed 19840 exact modular rank comparisons for every subset in 25 small-parameter cases over two independent primes; finite tests do not establish the general theorem.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the all-parameter if-and-only-if independently actuated vertex-subset classification and its explicit full counting polynomial for one exceptional edge. Prior PBH/maximum-multiplicity and zero-forcing theories provide general tools and bounds, not the required rank-one symmetry-breaking eigenspace computation and exact placement polynomial. The inspected bipartite spectral literature addresses other perturbations/observables. A review of actual distinct historical claims on weighted matching defects and two-clique barbell controls confirms neither logically implies this one-link criterion. Residual risk of equivalent specialized literature remains.
residual_risks: A specialized unpublished/unindexed exact calculation of weighted complete-bipartite controllability may already exist.

The general maximum-eigenvalue-multiplicity framework and elementary spectral algebra make the formula reproducible; novelty is the explicit closed all-set classification, not general PBH, symmetry reduction, or the fact that symmetry breaking can improve controllability.

value.rationale: All placement counts at every actuator budget are computed for a natural dense network whose support remains complete for c>0. A one-edge conductance defect reduces minimum actuator number by exactly two for unequal part sizes and one for equal part sizes; the homogeneous point is a sharp discontinuity and an exact boundary for the gap to zero forcing. This is a complete natural classification rather than a test on an arbitrary small instance or a routine single placement. Limits on control energy and ill-conditioning are explicitly left open.
